name: IANA JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) Algorithms
mergedIntoNote: Claims no path of its own because the adapter reading it names the HTTP status registry
as its primary, and the format credits a table to one source. `internet.jwt_algorithm`
comes from here; `internet.http_status_code.*` comes from the other; both are attributed
Declared rather than left as a warning nobody can resolve -- the alternative is splitting
one adapter into two for an attribution distinction the binary format cannot carry.
note: An IANA registry: the definition of the thing, not a copy of it. A status code is 404
because this file says so, and there is no locale, no opinion and no editorial
No licence, and none needed. IANA maintains these registries as a matter of record
under the IETF's process; the assignments are facts about the protocol rather than
authored work, in the same way the root zone's list of delegated TLDs is. See
LICENSES/iana-tld.txt for the same reasoning at more length.
IANA re-exports these CSVs on every registry change rather than versioning them, so the
integrity hash pins the content at the moment it was verified. A change upstream fails
the build, which is the intended behaviour: a new status code should be a deliberate
re-pin rather than a silent drift in what the corpus generates.
